name: osTicket - Email Harvesting & Sensitive Data Exposure
command: # 1) create a ticket at /open.php -> get a company email  2) reuse leaked creds at /scp/login.php  3) read tickets for leaked passwords
description: osTicket has few direct CVEs, so it is abused for what it exposes: submitting a ticket assigns a valid company email (usable to register on other gated services like Slack/GitLab), and reusing credentials harvested via OSINT (Dehashed) to log into the staff panel reveals passwords leaked inside support tickets - a classic sensitive-data-exposure chain.

steps.label: Step 1 - fingerprint osTicket (OSTSESSID cookie, 'powered by osTicket' footer)
Step 2 - open a ticket to get assigned a valid internal company email
Step 3 - harvest leaked credentials for the domain via OSINT
Step 4 - reuse creds at the staff/agent login (accepts username OR email)
Step 5 - read open/closed tickets for leaked passwords (new-joiner / reset passwords)
steps.command: # Dashboard -> Tickets -> read agent replies; export the address book of emails/usernames

steps.label: Step 6 - reuse the leaked password against exposed portals (e.g. VPN)
steps.command: # spray the standard/new-joiner password vs vpn.<domain>; build a userlist with linkedin2username

examples.label: Dehashed cleartext creds (fictional sample from the module)
examples.command:
jclayton:JulieC8765!
kgrimes:Fish1ng_s3ason!   # login worked as kevin@inlanefreight.local

examples.label: Subdomains found alongside - support + vpn are live
examples.command:
support.inlanefreight.local
vpn.inlanefreight.local   # Barracuda SSL VPN, no MFA

notes: osTicket 1.14.1 has CVE-2020-24881 (SSRF) but the module's taught path is abuse, not a CVE: (1) a submitted ticket hands you a real company email address to pass email-verification on other services; (2) the staff login at /scp/login.php accepts an email OR a username, so a Dehashed hit that fails as a username may succeed as the email; (3) inside the queue, agents frequently leak the standard new-joiner/reset password in a ticket reply - reuse it against the VPN. Also export the address book (emails/usernames) to feed password spraying. Root causes: external exposure, no MFA, password reuse, emailing passwords. Not an OSCP-listed app, so no OffSec reference is claimed.

references.title: Intigriti - Hacking companies through their helpdesk

recommended.note: The screenshot sweep that flags the osTicket instance to attack.
Reuse harvested creds/emails against other exposed apps.

defense.prerequisites: An externally exposed osTicket portal that allows ticket creation, plus either leaked/reused credentials (OSINT) or sensitive data sitting in the ticket queue. Staff login reachable at /scp/login.php.
defense.why_it_works: Helpdesk workflows assign real, routable company email addresses to tickets and store free-form agent replies; combined with password reuse and the login accepting email-or-username, an attacker turns public support functionality into a credential and data-access foothold.
defense.misconfiguration: Portal exposed externally without MFA; agents email/store passwords in tickets; corporate emails reused on third-party services; weak/standard new-joiner passwords not force-changed.
defense.impact: A valid company email for bypassing email verification elsewhere, staff-panel access via reused creds, and leaked passwords (e.g. VPN) enabling a network foothold - a stepping stone to internal access.
defense.detection: Staff logins from unusual IPs/geos; a single account trying username then email; bulk ticket reads/exports; new external account registrations tied to a ticket email; spray attempts against the VPN shortly after portal access.
defense.artifacts: osTicket auth logs (successful staff login, new IP); ticket-view/export events; VPN auth logs showing the leaked password; Dehashed queries are attacker-side (no target artifact).
defense.prevention: Enforce MFA on all external portals. Never send passwords through tickets. Ban corporate-email signups on third-party services. Enforce a strong AD/app password policy and force change-at-first-login. Limit what is exposed externally. [MITRE M1032, M1017, M1027]
defense.evasion: Blend in: create a normal-looking ticket, authenticate with valid creds (looks legitimate), and pace VPN spraying under lockout thresholds (osTicket account lockout / VPN throttling).
